title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 27-28
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 27 to 28 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'असङ्ख्येयोऽप्रमेयात्मा विशिष्टः शिष्टकृच्छुचिः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 27 to 28 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 27 to 28.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 27 to 28** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **असङ्ख्येयोऽप्रमेयात्मा विशिष्टः शिष्टकृच्छुचिः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**असङ्ख्येयोऽप्रमेयात्मा विशिष्टः शिष्टकृच्छुचिः । सिद्धार्थः सिद्धसङ्कल्पः सिद्धिदः सिद्धिसाधनः ॥** **वृषाही वृषभो विष्णुर्वृषपर्वा वृषोदरः । वर्धनो वर्धमानश्च विविक्तः श्रुतिसागरः ॥**

Countless, immeasurable and the most distinguished is he. The one who shapes the good and is ever pure is that God of gods. His resolve always comes true; he gives success and he is the way to it. He carries dharma as his banner, he is dharma in form. Strong as the bull, Vishnu, is that God of gods. Dharma is his very foundation. He makes all things grow, he grows, and he is the ocean of the Vedas.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 27 to 28 mean?
faq.a: Countless, immeasurable and the most distinguished is he. The one who shapes the good and is ever pure is that God of gods. His resolve always comes true; he gives success and he is the way to it. He carries dharma as his banner, he is dharma in form. Strong as the bull, Vishnu, is that God of gods. Dharma is his very foundation. He makes all things grow, he grows, and he is the ocean of the Vedas.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
